data.title: Choose the sentence that uses the word correctly.

sections.title: career
sections.question: career
sections.summary: the series of jobs a person has in their working life

senses.definition: the series of jobs that someone has during their working life, especially in one area of work
examples: She chose a career in medicine because she wanted to help people.
He has had a long career in teaching.

answers.answer: She built a successful career in nursing over twenty years.
He cooked a career for dinner and served it with vegetables.
She planted her career in the garden and watered it each morning.
They drove the career to the airport and left it in the car park.

sections.title: colleague
sections.question: colleague
sections.summary: a person who works with you in the same organisation

senses.definition: a person who works with you in the same organisation or department
examples: She had lunch with her colleague from the sales department.
He asked a colleague to help him with the new project.

answers.answer: She sent an email to her colleague about the project deadline.
He ordered a colleague from an online shop and waited for delivery.
She put her colleague on the shelf next to the books.
They cooked a colleague in the kitchen and served it with salad.

sections.title: company
sections.question: company
sections.summary: a business organisation that sells goods or services

senses.definition: a business organisation that makes or sells goods or provides a service
examples: She works for a technology company in the city centre.
The company employs over five hundred people.

answers.answer: She works for a large company that makes computers and software.
He ate a company for lunch with some bread and cheese.
She planted the company in the garden and watered it every day.
They drove the company to the airport and put it on the plane.

sections.title: employment
sections.question: employment
sections.summary: the fact of having a paid job

senses.definition: the state of having a paid job, or the activity of giving people jobs
examples: She found employment as a nurse after finishing her studies.
The new factory will bring employment to the area.

answers.answer: She found employment as a teacher after she graduated from university.
He cooked the employment for dinner and served it with rice.
She planted employment in the garden near the fence.
They drove the employment to the office and left it at the desk.

sections.title: interview
sections.question: interview
sections.summary: a meeting where someone asks you questions to see if you are right for a job

senses.definition: a formal meeting in which someone asks you questions to find out if you are suitable for a job or course
examples: She prepared carefully for her job interview the next morning.
He was very nervous before the interview, but it went well.

answers.answer: She wore smart clothes and practised her answers before the interview.
He ate the interview for lunch at his desk.
She cooked the interview in the oven and served it hot.
They planted an interview in the garden and waited for it to grow.

sections.title: job
sections.question: job
sections.summary: the regular work that you do to earn money

senses.definition: the regular work that a person does to earn money
examples: She found a new job as a receptionist at a large hotel.
He has a job at the supermarket on weekday evenings.

answers.answer: She found a new job as a receptionist at a hotel in the city.
He cooked a job for dinner and served it with salad.
She planted a job in the garden next to the rose bush.
They drank a glass of job every morning before work.

sections.title: manager
sections.question: manager
sections.summary: a person who is responsible for running a business, team, or department

senses.definition: a person who is responsible for running a business, team, or department
examples: She reported the problem to her manager at the office.
He was promoted to manager after five years with the company.

answers.answer: She asked her manager for permission to take a day off work.
He parked his manager next to his bicycle outside the office.
She put the manager in the oven and cooked it for an hour.
They watered the manager with a garden hose every morning.

sections.title: meeting
sections.question: meeting
sections.summary: an occasion when people come together to discuss something

senses.definition: an occasion when people come together to talk about or decide something
examples: She arrived early to prepare for the morning meeting.
The manager called a meeting to discuss the new project.

answers.answer: She printed the report before the meeting so everyone could read it.
He cooked a meeting in the kitchen for the whole team.
She planted a meeting in the garden and watered it twice a week.
They drank a meeting every morning before starting work.

sections.title: office
sections.question: office
sections.summary: a room or building where people work at desks

senses.definition: a room or building where people work, usually at desks in front of computers
examples: She spends most of her day in the office writing reports.
He goes to the office five days a week.

answers.answer: She goes to the office every day and answers emails at her desk.
He goes to the office to buy fresh vegetables every Saturday.
She swam across the office because it was a warm afternoon.
They drove the office to the station and left it on the platform.

sections.title: profession
sections.question: profession
sections.summary: a type of job that requires special training or education

senses.definition: a type of job that requires special training or education, such as medicine, law, or teaching
examples: Medicine is a challenging profession that requires many years of study.
She entered the teaching profession after university.

answers.answer: Teaching is a profession that requires patience and good communication skills.
He cooked a profession for dinner and served it with bread.
She planted her profession in the garden and waited for it to grow.
They drove the profession to the airport and checked it in as luggage.
